in human cutaneous Leishmania braziliensis infection:

the frequency of activated, memory, and antigen specific, cytokines producing lymphocytes are positively correlated with one another, suggesting that the frequency of these populations may reflect the magnitude of the immune response.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a detailed study of antigen specific T cell responses in the context of the disease can lead to a better understanding of mechanisms for the regulation of the immune response in leishmaniasisis.
a positive correlation between CD45RO expression and the frequency and magnitude of antigen specific IFN‐gamma production is indicative of protective immunity.
